newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares cautious but confident.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares cautious but confident.

text.p: Fresh Wall Street losses steered the Bel-20 index of leading shares to an 0.81 percent lower close on Monday but traders were confident that the Brussels bourse's correction would be modest.
"It's between a healthy consolidation and a small correction. There is no panic, we stay calm," said analyst Patrick Millecam at Antwerp brokerage Corluy.
The Bel-20, which had quickly recovered from opening losses, weakened again after New York's mid-afternoon opening and eventually shed 16.62 points at 2,043.99.
Millecam said that European bourses still looked relatively cheap in view of the current low level of interest rates and the strong dollar. "Rates have not been fully discounted yet."
A new political scandal over the arrest of two francophone socialist party officials linked to bribery had no impact. "It's really a non-event," Millecam said.

Dealers said that the Bel-20 should get support in the near term from institutional buying of 'click funds', which guarantee investors the benefits of a rising index while protecting them from major index falls.
Total volume in Belgian shares was a considerable 3.5 billion francs.
Retailers GIB and Delhaize were among the day's leading losers with a 2.5 and 3.5 percent loss respectively. GIB ended at 1,555 francs and Delhaize at 1,920.
Generale Bank first jumped to a record high of 12,450 francs but then slipped 2.6 percent to 11,950.
